reviewContext.userProblem: ART works around five gaps: (A) no built-in YouTube read gateway; (B) fanout joins see only each branch's last output, so the speech-to-text transcript is read from a private cache file; (C) durable-queue pending returns one item and has no attempt cap; (D) youtube-collect cannot drop live, upcoming or long videos; (E) riela/media-download hard-codes yt-dlp inside the runtime.
requiredOutcomes: riela/youtube-gateway-read v1 provides subscriptions.list, videos.list, channels.list and playlistItems.list with pageToken/maxResults pagination. It is macOS-only, reads credentials only through the YOUTUBE_GATEWAY_* env allowlist, is validated, documented, and has a mock-scenario example.

fanout.includeStepOutputs adds stepOutputs to completed branch records for both same-workflow and toWorkflowId fanouts. Invalid ids fail validation. When the field is absent the join is byte-identical. The bound is 8,000,000 bytes. It has tests and a mock example.
durable-queue pending supports limit (items, itemsTruncated) and maxAttempts (exhausted, exhaustedCount). The default output is unchanged.
youtube-collect supports excludeLive and maxDurationSeconds and reports excluded {count, live, duration}. The default output is unchanged.

The mediaDownload contract is documented. media/yt-dlp-download v1 ships as a package container add-on in examples/video-pipeline-yt-dlp, and installs, validates and mock-runs. riela/media-download still runs, and validate warns with migration guidance.
nonGoals: No VERSION, rielaVersion, formula or release change. No change to the ART repository or to ~/.riela.
No YouTube write operations, no auto-pagination, no persistence schema change, no new add-on resolver, and no delegation from riela/media-download.
No change to the Package.swift or Package.resolved youtube-gateway pin.
constraints: Every swift build, swift test and swiftlint run uses arch -arm64 /bin/zsh -lc, with logs under tmp/youtube-processing-builtins/<planId>/.

All work happens in the same working directory on main. Workers create no worktrees, run no git write operations, record fresh-read pre/post SHA-256 for owned files, and redo edits after detecting drift.
Tests make no live network calls. Package installs in tests set HOME (and RIELA_WORKFLOW_HOME) to a tmp directory.
Code that uses YouTubeGatewayCore stays inside #if canImport(YouTubeGatewayCore); the parsing and validation layers are SDK-free.
Credentials never appear in source, docs, examples, outputs or diagnostics.
designDecisionsAndRationale: A uses the google-service typed-operation engine (operation + arguments, riela-owned request enum, client protocol) because pinned YouTubeGatewayCore 33006f3 exposes a typed YouTubeClient and no GraphQL schema catalog; registration, validation placement, macOS gating and docs/example layout follow notion/x-gateway-read. ContainerGatewayAddonExecutor does not apply because YouTube is linked in-process.

B derives stepOutputs only from durable child-session accepted outputs so resumed parents rebuild identical joins; includeStepOutputs is carried on WorkflowFanoutDispatchDirective at every construction site; the size bound equals the contextFrom bound (8,000,000 bytes).
B cross-workflow step ids are validated in CLI workflow validate, where FileSystemWorkflowCalleeResolver exists; Core validates shape and same-workflow ids.
C keeps pending a read-only transaction with the existing comparator; exhausted rows stay pending and are retired through finish.
D filters run after videos.list enrichment and apply to every record; excluded videos are not failures and are not replaced.

E uses the shipped package node-add-on mechanism (riela-package.json addons[] with container execution, projected to ~/.riela/addons/<ns>/<name>/<version>/) as the equivalent host-provided resolver instead of the unimplemented addon.json layout; riela/media-download keeps its implementation and only gains a validation warning.
intentionalTradeoffs: riela/media-download does not delegate to the container add-on, so existing ART runs need no container runtime, at the cost of two downloader implementations for one release.

Workflows outside the owning package that reference media/yt-dlp-download resolve at runtime through the shared store, but workflow validate requires package ownership or a dependency lock (existing behavior, covered by the migration docs).
youtube-gateway-read has no auto-pagination; callers pass pageToken.
youtube-collect may return fewer than maxPerChannel videos when filters exclude some.
W1/W2 plans share one working directory on main; concurrent whole-package builds may block on siblings, mitigated by the bounded shared-wave build protocol and serial integration repair.
supportedEdgeCases: includeStepOutputs naming a step that ran twice (latest accepted payload), a step that never ran (omitted), collect-partial failed branches (no stepOutputs), toWorkflowId fanouts with and without resumeStepId, and resume after a branch-terminal checkpoint.
durable-queue limit above the pending count, all rows exhausted (found false), limit plus maxAttempts combined, near-256 KiB requests triggering itemsTruncated, and an absent queue directory.
youtube-collect null durations kept, live plus over-long attributed to live only, explicit video references filtered, and excludeLive false alone emitting no excluded key.
youtube-gateway-read templated arguments, blank or non-allowlisted credential env, HTTP 401/403 quota/500 without body leakage, and Linux builds compiling with a policy error at execution.
yt-dlp-download cache hit, private/local host rejection, live stream and over-long rejection, the unsupported ytDlpPath option, and python3 absent (XCTSkip).
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Live YouTube API calls and live yt-dlp container downloads (tests use no network or container runtime).
YouTube write operations (subscription insert/delete) and automatic pagination.
Persistence schema changes, a new add-on resolver, or the addon.json scoped layout.
Linux execution of youtube-gateway-read beyond compiling and returning a policy error; the Linux build is review-only locally.
Edits to the ART repository, ~/.riela, running RielaApp instances, VERSION, rielaVersion, the Homebrew formula or a release.

sharedWaveBuildProtocol: Plans ypb-01 to ypb-08 carry an identical 'Shared-wave build protocol'. If build or test diagnostics are only in non-owned files, never edit, revert or reformat them: log a blocked-by-sibling row (file, first diagnostic, log path, UTC time), then make up to 6 foreground re-runs about 60 s apart. The SwiftPM '.build' lock message means wait for exit. Diagnostics in owned files are always the plan's to fix. A persistent block becomes a deferred-to-integration record and the worker stops. Serial repair follows the wave join, and integrationVerification is the authoritative gate.

acceptanceCriteria: pending without options returns exactly {found, identity, request}, unchanged from today; existing DurableQueueTests stay green unmodified.

pending with limit (integer 1-100) adds ordered items [{identity, request, attempts}] using the existing comparator plus itemsTruncated bounded by DurableQueueJournal.maximumBytes; identity equals items[0].identity.

pending with maxAttempts (1-1,000,000,000) excludes rows with attempts >= maxAttempts from selection and reports exhausted [{identity, attempts}] in identity-byte order plus exhaustedCount; completed rows are never exhausted.
Out-of-range or non-integer limit/maxAttempts, or either option on admit/attempted/finish, fail with durableQueueInvalid; pending on an absent queue directory creates no files.
docs/workflows/durable-queue.md documents limit and maxAttempts; Sources/RielaCLI/DurableQueueJournal.swift is unchanged.
